verdict: P031 r10 is a well-scoped, product-sound read-only cutover proposal that resolves all five prior PO issues with verifiable contracts and evidence gates. The read-only narrowing is the correct sequencing choice: it de-risks the transition by separating read migration from write transport. Two conditions remain before unconditional approval: (1) legacy expiry must not remove rollback before at least one write-path follow-up is available or the release owner explicitly waives this dependency in writing with a hard deadline for write restoration, and (2) the rollback drill in Phase 0d must have defined quantitative success criteria — not just a pass/fail checkbox.
summary: r10 addresses every r9 PO issue. Scope discipline is exceptional: the read-only boundary is unambiguous, non-goals are exhaustive, and the UI write prohibition is enforceable through static guards and a maintained UI file/type inventory. The operator write-path guide, per-run workflow-completion notes, approval diagnostic comprehension evidence, and mandatory dogfood edge coverage close the main gaps from r9. Metrics are concrete and measurable across both technical compliance and user-outcome dimensions. Rollout strategy is well-structured with feature flag, hold criteria, rollback criteria, and legacy expiry. The remaining product risks are: (a) a potential window where operators have neither rollback nor in-app writes if legacy expiry fires before write-path restoration, (b) report metadata-only classification as P1 may underestimate operator friction if report inspection is a frequent activity, (c) rollback drill lacks quantitative success criteria, (d) the actual CLI recipes for the operator write-path guide remain an open question that could stall Phase 0d, and (e) dogfood additional-evidence triggers have no detection mechanism for the release owner. Score reduced from prior round's 9 to 8 because r10's thoroughness surfaces a structural gap: the legacy expiry and follow-up timelines are independently well-specified but not coordinated — the proposal can reach a state where rollback is removed and write controls are still absent, and no gate prevents this.

issues.title: Legacy expiry may remove rollback before write-path follow-ups are available
issues.description: Legacy rollback code is removed within 10 business days of flag removal. P031-FOLLOWUP-UI-CONTROL-SURFACE states 'Draft starts before legacy rollback code expiry' but does not require the follow-up to be landed or implementation-ready. If the draft only starts before expiry but the follow-up takes weeks to ship, operators face a window with no rollback safety net and no in-app write capability. This is a product risk because it removes the escape hatch before the replacement is ready. The proposal's hold criteria and rollback criteria are thorough for the P031 scope itself, but do not account for the post-P031 transition gap.
issues.why_it_matters: The worst-case operator experience is: thin-read mode ships, flag is removed, legacy code is deleted 10 business days later, and the write-path follow-up is still in draft. The operator now has no in-app writes and no way to rollback. This undermines the trust the entire phased rollout strategy is designed to build.
issues.recommended_fix: Add a legacy expiry dependency clause: legacy code removal requires either (a) at least one write-path follow-up proposal (approval or control surface) is merged and gate-green, or (b) the release owner signs a dated waiver explicitly accepting the gap and setting a hard deadline for write-path availability.
issues.acceptance_criteria: Legacy expiry is gated on write-path availability or an explicit release-owner waiver with a dated write-restoration deadline.

issues.title: Report payload follow-up classified as P1 may underestimate operator regression
issues.description: P031 ships reports as metadata-only with payload availability indicators. The follow-up (P031-FOLLOWUP-REPORT-PAYLOAD) is P1 'report utility recovery'. If report inspection is a frequent operator activity, metadata-only is a tangible daily regression. The proposal mitigates with pre-dogfood communication and payload availability status in the Reports list, but classifying the restore as P1 signals it could wait indefinitely after the approval write-path and control surface follow-ups.
issues.why_it_matters: If operators drill into report payloads regularly, forcing them to raw filesystem access defeats the purpose of the thin UI migration. The P1 classification lacks justification from operator workflow frequency data.
issues.recommended_fix: Either elevate P031-FOLLOWUP-REPORT-PAYLOAD to P0 alongside the approval write path, or add an explicit statement that report payload inspection is a low-frequency operator activity with evidence from current usage patterns.
issues.acceptance_criteria: Report payload follow-up priority is justified by operator workflow data, or elevated to P0.

issues.title: Rollback drill has no quantitative success criteria
issues.description: Phase 0d requires a rollback drill or release-owner waiver but defines no success criteria for the drill itself. Without a target for time-to-rollback, state consistency assertions, or operator confirmation protocol, the drill cannot meaningfully fail. This weakens the rollback readiness evidence that Phase 3 depends on.
issues.why_it_matters: A rollback drill without criteria is a checkbox, not evidence. The proposal's own rollback_criteria define when to trigger rollback but not what successful rollback looks like.
issues.recommended_fix: Define rollback drill exit criteria: (a) max time from dogfood/thin-read to legacy mode (e.g., under 60 seconds), (b) state consistency assertion (no projection data loss, no stale truth visible after rollback), (c) operator confirms legacy surfaces are functional after rollback.
issues.acceptance_criteria: Rollback drill has defined time, consistency, and operator-confirmation criteria before Phase 0d exit.

issues.title: Operator write-path guide recipes are an unresolved dependency that could stall Phase 0d
issues.description: OQ-031-01 acknowledges that the actual CLI/MCP/automation command recipes for each removed write control are not yet authored. The guide is a Phase 0d exit gate and dogfood prerequisite. If recipes cannot be authored or validated in time, the entire dogfood timeline stalls. No minimum-viable fallback is defined.
issues.why_it_matters: The write-path guide is the bridge between a read-only UI and a viable operator workflow. A vague guide that says 'use MCP' without tool names, parameter shapes, and expected outputs fails the intent of PO-R9-01.
issues.recommended_fix: Define a minimum-viable guide format: for each removed control, name the MCP tool, list minimum required identifiers, and note expected output. Full step-by-step recipes can iterate after dogfood starts. This prevents Phase 0d from becoming a bottleneck.
issues.acceptance_criteria: A minimum-viable guide format is defined so Phase 0d can exit even without polished multi-step recipes.

issues.title: Dogfood additional-evidence triggers lack detection mechanism
issues.description: The dogfood population assumption is 1-3 operators with four additional evidence triggers defined for expanded usage. The triggers are well-specified but there is no mechanism for the release owner to detect when they fire. If a fourth operator starts using the thin UI or a new approval shape appears, the release owner needs to know before sign-off.
issues.why_it_matters: Triggers that no one checks are not triggers — they are aspirations. The release owner signs off on dogfood evidence; they need to know whether any trigger fired during the dogfood period.
issues.recommended_fix: Add a pre-sign-off checklist item where the release owner reviews whether any additional-evidence trigger has fired. This can be a manual check in the sign-off template rather than automated detection.
issues.acceptance_criteria: Phase 3 sign-off template includes explicit review of each additional-evidence trigger.

suggestions.title: Gate legacy expiry on write-path availability
suggestions.description: Make legacy code removal contingent on at least one write-path follow-up being merged, or require a dated release-owner waiver that explicitly accepts the gap and sets a hard deadline for write restoration. This prevents the worst-case scenario where operators lose both rollback and in-app writes simultaneously.

suggestions.title: Define a minimum-viable operator write-path guide format
suggestions.description: Specify that the minimum guide can be a table of removed-control to MCP-tool-name plus required identifiers, without full step-by-step recipes. This unblocks Phase 0d even if polished documentation takes longer. Full recipes can iterate after dogfood starts.

suggestions.title: Add rollback drill quantitative exit criteria
suggestions.description: Define max time-to-rollback, post-rollback state consistency assertions, and operator functional confirmation as drill pass/fail criteria. Without these, the drill cannot meaningfully fail and the evidence is weak.

assumptions.assumption: The operator who issued the binding correction continues to accept that the macOS UI will have no write controls during and after P031, until follow-up proposals restore them.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If operator expectations have shifted, the capability gap will surface as friction during dogfood. The per-run workflow-completion notes now capture this signal, which is the correct safety net.

assumptions.assumption: Viable external write paths already exist for all critical operations (run start, run cancel, approval resolution, stage retry) through the P029 MCP tools.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If any critical write operation has no working external path, the operator guide will expose the gap rather than create a path. This is a discovery risk gated at Phase 0d, not a proposal gap.

assumptions.assumption: All five stated dependencies (P027, P029, P041, P042, P043) remain stable and do not regress during P031 implementation.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Regression in any dependency blocks P031 at the same-tree prerequisite gate in Phase 3. The hold criteria cover this but the mitigation is binary (hold), not graduated.

assumptions.assumption: The 1-3 operator dogfood population is representative of the full operator base for this workflow family.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Minimal risk at current scale. Additional-evidence triggers provide automatic escalation if population grows. Two dogfood runs with mandatory edge coverage is appropriate for a small internal audience.

assumptions.assumption: Report metadata-only is an acceptable temporary state for the operator population.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If operators frequently need full report payloads to make decisions, metadata-only forces raw filesystem access, undermining the thin UI value. The P1 follow-up priority may need elevation — see PO-R10-02.

assumptions.assumption: The P043 reconciliation in Phase 0a can be completed without re-opening the P043 contract or requiring a new P043 review cycle.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If P043 reconciliation requires substantive re-review, Phase 0a takes significantly longer than the estimated 1.5-2.5 days. The phased structure contains this risk through Phase 0d re-estimation.

PO-R9-01.assessment: Operator write-path guide is now a Phase 0d deliverable with 100% removed-control coverage target, explicit mapping rules, minimum copy identifiers, and integration into first-run orientation and approval diagnostic banners.

PO-R9-02.assessment: Operator workflow viability is now a named metric requiring per-run workflow-completion notes stating whether the run completed end-to-end without improvised workarounds.

PO-R9-03.assessment: Follow-ups now have priority tiers and expected start timeframes. Approval write path is P0 immediate next, UI control surface is P1 before legacy expiry, report payload is P1 tied to dogfood friction.

PO-R9-04.assessment: Dogfood evidence now requires at least one approval diagnostics comprehension observation with binary diagnostic contract, banner/callout UI, and copyable identifiers.

PO-R9-05.assessment: Dogfood edge-case coverage is now mandatory: degraded-state recovery, approval diagnostics, Reports payload status, targeted read refresh, and metadata-only report inspection.
